text: Git branching is a core feature of version control. Instead of working directly on the main codebase, developers create feature branches. These are separate copies of the project where you can add new features or fix bugs without affecting the stable version. Once your work is complete, you can merge the branch back into the main line. Before merging, many teams use pull requests, which let others review your code and suggest changes. This workflow keeps the project organized, reduces conflicts, and makes collaboration safer. In short, branching gives you the freedom to experiment while protecting the quality of the main code.
